message.subject: You won ₱1,000,000
message.body: Congratulations! Your address was selected for ₱1,000,000. Claim within 10 minutes. Follow the link and confirm your account password to release the prize.
message.safety_label: FICTIONAL PRACTICE • No real links or credentials

intro.title: Morning light
intro.speaker: player
intro.text: My eyes slowly open. Morning light fills my room. Then I hear it... my phone is buzzing.

intro.title: Where is my phone?
intro.speaker: player
intro.text: I turn toward the sound and reach across the bed. There it is. A new notification lights up the screen.

intro.title: A new email
intro.speaker: player
intro.text: I unlock my phone. A message from Prize Desk is waiting for me.

intro.title: One tempting promise
intro.speaker: player
intro.text: I open the message. It asks me to follow a link and confirm my account password to claim the prize.

intro.title: What if it is real?
intro.speaker: player
intro.text: A million pesos. For a moment, I imagine it. Before checking who sent the offer, I tap Claim Prize.

intro.caption: And this is how it began…

amani.caption: Her phone has no signal. Her friends receive messages that appear to be hers. Someone is using the trust attached to her identity.

liza.caption: A familiar voice asked for a payment. It went to the wrong account. The attacker used a voice she had reason to recognize.

staff.caption: Her name approved a request for a confidential student list. She never approved it. The attacker borrowed her authority.

classmate.caption: A free offer led to lost account access. The attacker turned something appealing into a request for something private.

clues.title: Who sent it?
clues.note: The display name sounds official, but this address does not independently establish who is offering a prize.

clues.title: Where does it lead?
clues.note: The destination requests an account password. Do not use this link to verify the message that supplied it.

clues.title: Why the rush?
clues.note: The deadline pressures you to act before checking. Urgency is a clue to examine, not proof by itself.

clues.title: What is promised?
clues.value: ₱1,000,000 from a selection I did not enter
clues.note: An unexpected reward plus a password request is a reason to stop. A prize should not need your account password.

wake.title: That morning, again
wake.text: That message again. A million pesos… but why would they choose me? This time, I can stop and look.

inbox.title: One unread message
inbox.text: My phone is buzzing. I unlock it and open Mail. Reading an email is not the same as trusting its link.

choice.title: Before I act
choice.text: The offer sounds tempting. Do I claim it, delete it, or find out what this message is really asking for?

inspect_intro.title: A closer look
inspect_intro.text: Before I do anything, I'll look at what this message is asking me to believe—and what it wants me to do.

next_issue.title: One more thing
next_issue.text: I've noticed the promises and the pressure. Now I'll check who actually sent this message.

sender.title: Who is behind the name?
sender.text: Prize Desk sounds official, but a name is easy to copy. I will open the sender's full address.

notes.title: A note to remember
notes.text: I'll open Notepad and record the sender's domain. If I forget it, I can go back to Mail and check.

claim.title: A prize with a price
claim.text: The page wants my account password. Why would anyone need that to give me a prize? No real password belongs here.

failure.title: The secret was the target
failure.text: In this imagined ending, I gave the fake page a password. That could let an attacker access my account. Opening the email alone did not cause it. The deception was theirs; I can rewind and choose differently.

safe.title: No prize, no risk taken
safe.text: I deleted the request without sharing anything. That was a safe choice. But what did I miss? I can revisit a practice copy and investigate—or leave for now.

inspect.title: Look closer
inspect.text: What is the offer, why the rush, and what secret do they want? I will mark the clues and read the full sender address.

capture.title: Keep the context
capture.text: Drag the frame; its blue corner resizes. Keep the sender, subject and request together. TOOLS offers tap controls and Capture.

submit.title: Build the exhibit
submit.text: The message, the sender's domain, and my warning signs belong together. This is the practice desk: sending here stays inside the game.

sealed.title: Practice exhibit sealed
sealed.text: I kept my password private and preserved the evidence. I know what made this request unsafe—not just which button to press.

closing.title: A different morning
closing.text: If only John thought of this before....

summary.title: TUTORIAL COMPLETE
summary.text: You examined a request, recorded its sender, captured the context and sealed a practice exhibit. Your next story is still ahead. This tutorial awards no coins or mastery.
